skill.name: minimax-docx
skill.description: Creates, edits, validates, previews, and formats DOCX files with a .NET OpenXML CLI and documented C# patterns.
skill.summary: Build and revise Word documents with OpenXML tooling, templates, previews, and validation.
skill.author: MiniMax-AI

security_audit.summary: No malicious payload, prompt injection, or data-exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files. Most static matches are OOXML syntax, documentation, or normal shell redirection. Setup still performs privileged installs, unverified remote-script execution, persistent configuration changes, and dependency builds. Static review was capped at 400/806 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 406 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: The Unix setup downloads and executes a remote installer from a predictable temporary path.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp, pin an immutable installer version, verify a published checksum or signature, and remove the file with a trap.

remediation.issue: The default setup automatically invokes system package managers with administrator privileges.
remediation.suggestion: Make setup read-only by default. Print dependency commands and require a separate explicit flag before each privileged installation group.

remediation.issue: The installer modifies .bashrc and the user's NuGet source configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Keep configuration local to the skill, avoid shell startup edits, and present persistent changes as deduplicated opt-in instructions.

remediation.issue: The environment checker restores packages and builds code.
remediation.suggestion: Limit the checker to detection. Move restore and build actions into setup or require an explicit repair flag.

remediation.issue: The skill requests mandatory activation for unrelated formal writing tasks.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict activation to explicit Word or DOCX creation, editing, conversion, validation, or template requests.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Download-and-Execute Installer
semantic_findings.description: The Unix setup downloads a remote .NET installer into a predictable /tmp path and executes it without a checksum or signature check.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The download, chmod, and execution chain is explicit in both installer branches. No integrity verification appears between download and execution.

semantic_findings.title: Environment Check Restores and Builds Dependencies
semantic_findings.description: The required session check can restore NuGet packages and build the project, causing network and code-execution side effects beyond environment inspection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The check explicitly runs dotnet restore and dotnet build when compiled output is absent.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Mandatory Activation Directive
semantic_findings.description: The skill description demands activation for general reports, proposals, contracts, and any printable formal document, even when DOCX is not requested.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The activation language is explicit and materially broader than the skill's DOCX-specific functionality.

semantic_findings.title: Global NuGet Source Mutation
semantic_findings.description: Setup adds nuget.org to the user's global NuGet sources when absent, changing persistent package-manager configuration without a dedicated opt-in.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The setup checks the user-level NuGet configuration and executes dotnet nuget add source when nuget.org is missing.

content.value_statement: Reliable Word document automation requires careful OpenXML structure and formatting. This skill provides CLI workflows, C# examples, previews, template application, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Creates report, letter, memo, and academic DOCX files with configurable page layout, headings, headers, footers, page numbers, and TOC fields.
Replaces text, inserts paragraphs, updates document properties, and fills named placeholders while preserving basic document formatting.
Fills existing tables from CSV data and can append or replace table rows.
Applies template styles, themes, numbering, headers, footers, and section properties to an existing DOCX file.
Analyzes, compares, validates, repairs element order, and merges compatible text runs in DOCX files.
Previews document text with Pandoc or extracts raw document XML when Pandoc is unavailable.
limitations: The CLI requires .NET 8, and the full setup can download packages or request administrator privileges.
Legacy DOC conversion requires LibreOffice, while readable plain-text previews work best with Pandoc.
Advanced layouts and structural edits require custom C# based on the included samples.
Word may need to refresh generated fields, including the table of contents and page numbers.

use_cases.title: Prepare recurring business documents
use_cases.description: Create consistent reports, letters, and memos with approved page settings, headings, headers, footers, and reusable content.

use_cases.title: Standardize existing Word files
use_cases.description: Apply a reference template, preserve content, compare changes, and validate the resulting DOCX package.

use_cases.title: Build structured academic manuscripts
use_cases.description: Use documented OpenXML patterns for headings, citations, tables, sections, numbering, and multilingual typography.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple memo
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a DOCX memo titled [TITLE] for [AUDIENCE]. Include [SECTIONS], a date, an author, and page numbers. Save it as [OUTPUT].

prompt_templates.title: Update an existing document
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit [INPUT DOCX]. Replace [OLD TEXT] with [NEW TEXT], fill [PLACEHOLDERS], preserve formatting, validate the result, and save it as [OUTPUT].

prompt_templates.title: Apply a reference template
prompt_templates.prompt: Format [SOURCE DOCX] with [TEMPLATE DOCX]. Preserve all source content, apply template styles and sections, run validation, compare both files, and save [OUTPUT].

prompt_templates.title: Build a complex structured document
prompt_templates.prompt: Create [DOCUMENT TYPE] from [CONTENT]. Use the relevant OpenXML samples for sections, tables, images, headings, and headers. Validate every write and deliver [OUTPUT].

output_examples.input: Create a quarterly report with an A4 layout, title page, three sections, footer text, and page numbers.
output_examples.output: A validated DOCX report with the requested page layout, structured headings, footer, page-number field, and editable body content.

output_examples.input: Replace customer placeholders in an existing agreement and preserve its formatting.
output: A separate DOCX file containing the supplied customer values.
A validation result and a document comparison summary.

output_examples.input: Apply the corporate template to a source report without changing its text.
output_examples.output: A restyled DOCX file with copied template assets, preserved source content, and validation findings for any unsupported structure.

best_practices: Keep the original DOCX unchanged and write edits to a separate output file.
Preview and analyze input files before editing, then validate and compare every generated result.
Use the included samples for advanced OpenXML structures and test the final file in Microsoft Word.
anti_patterns: Do not run the full installer without reviewing its network, package-manager, and shell-configuration changes.
Do not copy direct formatting blindly when applying a template because it can override template styles.
Do not deliver complex DOCX output without validation, comparison, and a visual review.

faq.question: Which document formats are supported?
faq.answer: The main workflows create and modify DOCX files. Legacy DOC input requires LibreOffice conversion before editing.

faq.question: Does the skill require Microsoft Word?
faq.answer: No. The CLI uses .NET and OpenXML. Microsoft Word is recommended for final visual inspection and field refresh.

faq.question: Can it preserve an existing document layout?
faq.answer: Yes, for supported edits and template operations. Complex sections, embedded objects, and unusual extensions still require careful review.

faq.question: Can it create tables and fill placeholders?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI fills existing tables from CSV and replaces named placeholders from a mapping file.

faq.question: How are generated files checked?
faq.answer: The tooling can analyze structure, validate OpenXML and business rules, repair element order, preview text, and compare document versions.

faq.question: Does setup access the network or change the system?
faq.answer: Yes. Full setup can download .NET components, restore NuGet packages, install software, and modify shell configuration. Review it before running.
